steps.title: Import React and FC from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the FC (FunctionComponent) type from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and FC from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and FC from 'react'
import React, { FC } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and FC from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports to create TypeScript React components.
successCriteria: The import statement should import React and FC from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the FC type, which are essential for creating TypeScript React components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both React and FC from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and FC from 'react'.

steps.title: Create interface for component props
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named GreetingProps that defines the props your component will accept. The interface should have a required 'name' property of type string and an optional 'message' property of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and curly braces. Inside, define 'name: string' and 'message?: string'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a GreetingProps interface with the required 'name' and optional 'message' properties properly typed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the GreetingProps interface with the correct property types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your interface has both the required 'name' property and optional 'message' property with the correct TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'GreetingProps', and include both properties with proper TypeScript types.

steps.title: Create component with typed props
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Greeting that accepts GreetingProps as its props and returns a simple JSX element (like a <div> with a greeting message).
steps.hint: Use either a function declaration or arrow function. The component should accept props typed with the GreetingProps interface you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Greeting component is created that accepts typed props and returns JSX.
successCriteria:
The component should be named Greeting, accept GreetingProps, and return JSX (like a
or

element).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed functional component. The Greeting component now accepts props according to the GreetingProps interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure: 1) The component is named Greeting, 2) It accepts GreetingProps as its props type, and 3) It returns some JSX element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've created a functional component named Greeting that accepts GreetingProps and returns JSX.

steps.title: Display props in component
steps.instruction: Inside the Greeting component, return JSX that displays the name prop value. Use the prop value inside curly braces.
steps.hint: Access the prop value using the props parameter (e.g., props.name) and embed it in JSX with curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component now displays the name prop value in the UI.
successCriteria: Prop value is displayed inside curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the name prop value in the component's JSX.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the prop value inside curly braces in the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't displaying the prop value yet. Remember to access the prop (e.g., props.name) and embed it in JSX with curly braces.

steps.title: Add default values with logical OR operator
steps.instruction: Inside your Greeting component, modify the props to use the logical OR operator (||) to provide a fallback value when the 'name' prop is undefined. Use 'Guest' as the fallback value.
steps.hint: You can use the logical OR operator directly in the JSX where you display the prop value. For example: {props.name || 'Guest'}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display 'Guest' when the name prop is not provided, using the logical OR operator to handle undefined values.
successCriteria: The component should use the logical OR operator (||) with 'Guest' as the fallback value when displaying the name prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a fallback value using the logical OR operator. This ensures your component displays 'Guest' when the name prop is undefined.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the logical OR operator (||) with 'Guest' as the fallback value in the JSX where you display the name prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet use the logical OR operator to provide a fallback value. Try adding {props.name || 'Guest'} in the JSX where you display the name prop.

steps.title: Create App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element.
steps.hint: Define a new component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. It should return a JSX element like a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new App component that can serve as the parent component to test Greeting components.
successCriteria: The App component is defined with a name of 'App' and returns a JSX element (like a div).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component. This will serve as the parent component where we'll render our Greeting components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your App component is properly defined with a name of 'App' and returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component wasn't created correctly. Make sure you define a component named 'App' that returns a JSX element.

steps.title: Render Greeting with all props
steps.instruction: In the App component, render a Greeting component and pass the name prop with a string value.
steps.hint: Use the Greeting component like a JSX element and provide the name prop as an attribute.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of rendering a component with props
<MyComponent name="Alice" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render the Greeting component with a name prop provided.
successCriteria: The Greeting component is rendered inside App's JSX with a name prop attribute containing a string value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the Greeting component with the required name prop.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering the Greeting component inside App's return statement and passing a name prop with a string value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Greeting component isn't being rendered with the required name prop. Check that you're using the Greeting component in App's JSX and providing the name attribute.

steps.title: Render Greeting with missing optional prop
steps.instruction: In the App component, add a second Greeting component that only passes the required name prop (without the optional prop).
steps.hint: Add another <Greeting name="..." /> component inside the App's return JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will now render two Greeting components: one with all props and one with only the required name prop.
successCriteria: Pass only the name prop to it
Place it inside the App's return JSX
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a second Greeting component with only the required name prop. This will help demonstrate how default values work when optional props are omitted.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a second Greeting component with only the name prop. Check that it's inside the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add another Greeting component inside the App's return statement, passing only the name prop (like <Greeting name="..." />).

steps.title: Define defaultProps object
steps.instruction: Add a static defaultProps property to the Greeting component to provide default values for its props.
steps.hint: After the Greeting component definition, add Greeting.defaultProps = { ... } with the appropriate default values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component now has a defaultProps property that provides default values for its props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the defaultProps property to the Greeting component. This is the traditional React way to define default values for props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've correctly defined the defaultProps property on the Greeting component with the appropriate default values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The defaultProps property wasn't added correctly. Make sure to add Greeting.defaultProps = { ... } after the component definition, with the appropriate default values for the props.

steps.title: Update component to use defaultProps
steps.instruction: In the Greeting component, remove the logical OR operator fallback from the JSX and instead directly display the props.name value. The default fallback will now be handled by defaultProps.
steps.hint: Replace the comment inside the div with just {props.name} without any || operator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component will now display props.name directly, relying on defaultProps to provide a fallback value when the prop is not passed.
successCriteria: No fallback value in the JSX
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've removed the logical OR fallback from the component. Now the component will rely on defaultProps to provide default values when props are missing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've completely removed the logical OR operator (||) and are displaying props.name directly without any fallback value in the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: It looks like you still have the logical OR operator in your JSX. Remove the || operator and display props.name directly instead.

steps.title: Test defaultProps behavior
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, add a third Greeting component that only passes the name prop (omit the optional prop) to test that defaultProps provides the fallback value.
steps.hint: Add a new <Greeting> element with only the name attribute, similar to the existing ones but without the optional prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will now have three Greeting components rendered, with the third one testing that defaultProps provides values when optional props are omitted.
successCriteria: Place it inside the existing <div> in App
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a third Greeting component that only passes the name prop. This will help us test the defaultProps behavior in the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding a third Greeting component with only the name prop inside the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add a third Greeting component inside the App component's return statement, passing only the name prop (like name="Test").

steps.title: Export App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be rendered by React.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax to make the App component available for import in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it ready to be rendered by React.
successCriteria: The code includes 'export default App;' after the App component definition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the App component as the default export. This makes it available for React to render.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using 'export default App;' exactly after the App component definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't exported correctly. Use 'export default App;' to make it the default export.
